cases.question: Was the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread wider on 2026-07-09 than on 2026-06-09?

cases.keyFigures:
Nearby dated observations found (no exact match for 06-09 or 07-09): GuruFocus reports the spread 
was 2.75 as of 2026-06-03
. Convex/FRED reports it 
was 278 bps (2.78%), last updated June 25, 2026
, and MacroRadar cites a 
latest reading of 2.80 percent as of June 2026 (data through 2026-06-29)
. A StockCharts market commentary published right at the July 1 mark referenced 
280 basis points on the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread
 and noted 
HY and IG credit spreads are tame, but they have crept higher as stocks have wobbled in recent weeks
. Then govspending.org shows it 
was 2.75 Percent as of July 2, 2026
, and YCharts/Convex show it at 
2.74% for Jul 03 2026

cases.evidenceSummary: The available data shows the spread hovering in a very tight 2.74%–2.80% band across the June 3 – July 3, 2026 window, with a modest rise from ~2.75% (June 3) to ~2.78–2.80% (June 25–29), then easing back to ~2.74–2.75% by July 2-3. Since June 9 falls near the low end of this range (likely ~2.75-2.76%) and July 9 falls just after the July 3 reading of 2.74% (likely similarly ~2.73-2.75%), the two values appear to be very close to each other, with a slight lean toward July being flat-to-lower rather than wider. However, without the exact closing prints for 2026-06-09 and 2026-07-09 specifically, the outcome cannot be confirmed with full certainty given how narrow the day-to-day moves are in this series.

cases.question: Did a major hyperscaler or AI lab announce a new dedicated power-generation or power-purchase agreement for AI/data-center capacity between 2026-06-09 and 2026-07-09?
cases.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if at least one announcement of a new dedicated power-generation project or power-purchase agreement for AI/data-center capacity by a major hyperscaler (e.g. Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta) or AI lab was made between 2026-06-09 and 2026-07-09 (check energy trade press and company announcements). Resolves NO if none. Name the specific deal(s), parties, and announcement date(s).
cases.keyFigures: Chevron Corp (via subsidiary Energy Forge One LLC) announced on June 22, 2026 a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft Corp. to build a co-located natural gas power facility ("Project Kilby") in West Texas, expected to deliver approximately 2.67 GW of capacity, primarily via GE Vernova turbines with additional Solar Turbines (Caterpillar) units; first power delivery anticipated in 2028, Chevron Final Investment Decision expected by end of 2026 (Chevron Newsroom, June 22, 2026). Separately, DCD's grid-level news tracker also lists a Google PPA-related deal (Voltus supplying capacity to Google operations across the PJM grid) reported around June 1-3, 2026, just outside/at the edge of the window, and multiple other prior 2026 deals (Meta-Vistra nuclear PPA in January 2026, Google-TotalEnergies Texas solar PPAs in February 2026, Meta-Louisiana Hyperion gas expansion and Google-Crusoe Texas gas plant reported early April 2026) established the ongoing trend but predate the window.
cases.evidenceSummary: The Chevron-Microsoft "Project Kilby" 20-year dedicated power purchase agreement, announced June 22, 2026, directly satisfies the resolution criteria: it is a new dedicated power-generation/PPA deal for AI/data-center capacity, involves a major hyperscaler (Microsoft), and falls within the June 9–July 9, 2026 window. This is a specific, named, dated deal reported by both Chevron's own newsroom and independent press (TechCrunch reference to the broader trend), meeting the bar for a clear YES resolution.
